content:
maya: Heads-up — after the priority routing tweak rolled out to 5% canary, we saw an SSE p95 latency wobble in eu-west.
aj: Which tweak specifically? the route-priority fallback or the probe pacing change?
maya: route-priority fallback. We moved tenant-pref to higher priority so short-lived probes got re-routed more aggressively. Timeline: 10:04 canary start, 10:07 p95 spike.
shreya: Do we have a clear signal that it's routing rather than backend load? any correlation with connection churn?
maya: Quick diffs:
- sse.probe.pacing.rate increased by ~3x for affected tenants
- route.swap.count up ~12% during spike
- backend CPU steady
aj: paste of the most relevant log excerpt:
```
[10:07:12] route-switch: tenant=acme id=primary->fallback reason=probe_paced
[10:07:12] sse: conn_id=abcd reconnects=2 probe_delay_ms=120
[10:07:13] metrics: sse.probe.pacing.rate=0.31 -> 0.95
```
sam: That probe_paced reason is from the new pacing heuristic. It was supposed to avoid hitting quota windows, but looks like it caused more re-routes and short-term load on fallback pools.
console-team: Our dashboard sampling for SSE events is at 1% by default — the spike is barely visible except in derived p95. We probably under-sample probe churn.
shreya: Under-sampling explains why ops missed early signals. If probes are cheap but frequent, sampling amplifies aliasing.
maya: Proposal:
1) Add a transient telemetry override when route-priority changes — bump SSE sampling to 10% for 15m for the impacted route-id.
2) Introduce a small "grace_smooth_ms" on routing decisions so we don't flip routes on probe bursts: default 200ms.
3) Add metadata tag "probe-only" on the fallback route so console and billing treat probe traffic separately (avoid quota double-counting).
aj: Quick config sketch for the grace smoothing (WIP):
```
routing:
  priority_policy: tenant_pref
  fallback:
    grace_smooth_ms: 200
    probe_only_tag: true
```
sam: For rollouts: feature-flag path: sse_grace_smoothing_v2. Start at 0.1% -> 1% -> 5% -> 25% -> 100%, monitor sse.probe.pacing.rate and route.swap.count. Do not enable automatic quota billing until probe_only_tag is in place.
shreya: Concern: if we tag fallback as probe-only, we must ensure tenant quotas and billing don't consider fallback traffic as user tokens. That needs a guard in the metering pipeline.
infra-bot: FYI queued deploy: routing-service:feature/smoothing -> staging at 11:20. CI green.
deploy-bot: Canary roll triggered for sse_grace_smoothing_v2=0.1% at 11:25. Watchlist created: dashboard link https://console.redwood/test/dashboards/sse-probe-pacing
console-team: I'll temporarily increase sample rate for that dashboard and add an alert: when route.swap.count increases >10% over baseline AND p95>200ms for 5m.
aj: Action items summary:
- sam: add probe_only_tag + metering guard (PR)
- maya: flip console sampling override for 15m during canary
- shreya: validate that grace_smooth_ms prevents flip-flop in tests
- infra: run the canary and collect 30m traces
- console-team: add alert and short-lived sampling bump
maya: Thanks — let's reconvene in the canary channel if we see more than 3 route flips/min. :thinking_face:
